results.title: Nebius AI Cloud: Q3 2026 updates
results.author: Narek Tatevosyan
highlights:
Nebius AI Cloud: Q3 2026 updates

What we built this quarter: Nebius Cloud Platform

October 1, 2026

Listening to customers helps shape what we build next. As they scale training and inference, their priorities extend beyond just GPU performance: connecting workloads to existing systems, keeping control of resources and costs, and helping teams move faster.

Those priorities shaped our Q3 work on the cloud platform: the infrastructure and tooling layer of the Nebius AI Cloud. Here’s a look back at what we built, from private connectivity, updated demand-based GPU pricing to simpler ways for developing and running workloads.

...

## Control AI spend and make better use of capacity Control AI spend and make better use of capacity

As more teams share an AI platform, understanding consumption becomes as important as provisioning resources, especially with current market conditions. Customers need to know which workloads generate costs and how shared capacity is allocated.

Last year, we introduced our Preemptible Virtual Machines (PVMs) instances offering. PVMs run short-term, flexible workloads on platform capacity that is already allocated but sitting idle. Adoption came quickly, including among Serverless AI users. In a market where GPU capacity is limited, pulling more usable compute out of every deployed GPU creates more AI value from the same energy input, at a significantly reduced price for the user.

This quarter we announced Spot pricing for PVMs, that sets pricing dynamically and algorithmically, reflecting real demand for a specific GPU type in a specific Nebius region. The current price and up to 30 days of history are visible. We think this benefits everyone: cost-sensitive teams can see when a pool is typically quiet and schedule flexible work into those windows, and teams that care more about finishing than saving can follow the price and keep running.

Other new features help organizations be more in control of usage. Cost allocation labels let organizations attribute spending across teams, projects and environments using their existing labeling structure. A monthly usage and cost breakdown provides a downloadable PDF for accounting and reconciliation. Project limits for Capacity Block Groups let administrators control how much of a reserved pool each project can consume, preserving capacity for other teams.

...

This blog covers the cloud platform layer of that work. For everything we delivered across Nebius AI Cloud — including managed inference with Token Factory and agentic search with Tavily — explore our Q3 What’s New page.

results.title: Nebius achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on NVIDIA HGX B300 for training
results.author: Nebius team
highlights:
Nebius achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on NVIDIA HGX B300 for training

Nebius achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on NVIDIA HGX B300 for training workloads

October 8, 2026

Nebius has achieved NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on NVIDIA HGX B300 for training workloads. NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud recognizes cloud platforms that meet NVIDIA’s performance requirements across a defined suite of AI workloads. NVIDIA validated our production infrastructure using its Performance Benchmarking recipes, evaluating training performance against its reference architecture.

This achievement follows our Exemplar Cloud validations on NVIDIA H200 and NVIDIA HGX GB300 NVL72.

...

Cloud providers run NVIDIA’s standardized benchmarking recipes, measure results against its reference performance, and submit those results to NVIDIA for review. Nebius and NVIDIA engineers tested our production infrastructure, reviewed the results, and refined the platform configuration.

Each GPU platform requires its own validation. Achieving Exemplar on HGX B300 extends our work with the NVIDIABlackwell Ultra platform available on Nebius AI Cloud. This result builds on the engineering approach behind our Exemplar validation on NVIDIA H200 and NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 achievements: designing, operating, and optimizing hardware and cloud software together for customer workloads.

## What repeat external validation means for training on Nebius What repeat external validation means for training on Nebius

Exemplar is a strong signal that Nebius’ HGX B300 infrastructure is ready for the most demanding production training workloads, backed by NVIDIA’s validation of training performance. For customers planning demanding training runs, the external validation provides greater confidence in the platform, supported by measured workload performance.

Beyond Exemplar, separate evaluations provide additional evidence of our infrastructure’s performance and reliability. In MLPerf® Training 6.0, Nebius posted the fastest single-node NVIDIA HGX B300 times for Llama-3.1-8B and GPT-OSS 20B in the closed division. SemiAnalysis recently rated Nebius Platinum in ClusterMAX™ 3.0, its highest tier, following testing of training and inference workloads, storage, and failure recovery on live NVIDIA HGX B300 and GB300 NVL72 clusters.

results.title: Open-source NVIDIA Run:ai is now available on Nebius AI Cloud Applications
results.author: David Schulman
highlights:
The full NVIDIA Run:ai platform, a component of NVIDIA DSX OS™ within the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, is now open source. NVIDIA Run:ai is a Kubernetes-native platform for AI workload and GPU orchestration, with capabilities including fractional GPU allocation, gang scheduling, and team-level quotas that let many teams share one cluster without stepping on each other.

As a launch partner for the release, Nebius has made open-source NVIDIA Run:ai available in Nebius AI Cloud Applications, running on Nebius Service for Managed Kubernetes. Together, Nebius provides high-performance NVIDIA accelerated infrastructure and managed Kubernetes, while NVIDIA Run:ai adds the workload and GPU orchestration needed to allocate that infrastructure dynamically across teams and workloads. This gives AI builders a streamlined way to deploy workloads, improve GPU utilization, and increase throughput.

results.title: Nebius acquires Inferize to strengthen Nebius Token Factory's production inference stack
highlights:
Cold starts — the time models need to load before serving a single request — impose additional time and costs on teams running AI models in production at scale. This leaves assigned GPUs idle at launch time, when demand spikes and new instances spin up, and when weights are updated mid-run for example during reinforcement learning — and forces platforms to hold spare capacity just to hit their service-level targets.

Inferize’s technology cuts this “idle GPU tax”, enabling capacity to scale much more closely with actual usage and driving higher capacity utilization and better token economics.
